summary: Little Stone Mountain watchtowers near Big Stone Gap from the 1910s; the later CCC iron tower was torn down in the 1970s and its parts reportedly lie on private land.

facts.design: Iron tower with an iron cab, built by the Civilian Conservation Corps; the earlier tower was wooden
facts.status_note: Torn down in the 1970s; a 2019 local history places its parts on private cabin land.

access.note: The parts reportedly lie on private cabin property atop Morris's Butt, per a 2019 local history. Ask the owner before going near.

facts.agency: Virginia Forestry Department, later Jefferson National Forest

events.note: Start of the 1910 to 1917 window for the first watchtower on Little Stone Mountain. The exact date is not known, and the site is only the author's best guess.
By 1917 the tower had been moved to the ridge top of Little Stone Mountain, where a second tower was built with the state forestry department.
Iron tower built by the Civilian Conservation Corps on National Forest land. The author gives no exact date and believes it went up not long after 1933.
Torn down in the 1970s. The account gives no exact year; 1970 marks only the start of that decade.

notes_for_editor: The main source is one self-published local history (Fleenor, 2019), a personal account with few citations. Its title claim, first fire tower in Virginia, is the author's. Dates are windows or approximations: 1910 to 1917 for the first tower, not long after 1933 for the CCC tower, and the 1970s for removal (1970 is a placeholder year). The first tower's builder and site are not documented; the story gives only the author's guesses. The FFLA point 36.89721, -82.73853 is not checked against the old sites. The FFLA unconfirmed list also flags Little Stone Mountain (same as Stonega?) as a possible duplicate. The Hiking Project photo gives only 'near Big Stone Gap'. The PDF's bare-domain host has a certificate error; the www host serves the same file. Fact-check 2026-10-21: story corrected for an unsupported 'timber firm' attribution, an unsupported 'access is private' inference, a 'visitor's' photo label, a claim that the author did not know where the first tower stood (the account gives a best guess), and 'ran' a store (the account says owned).
